sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，与商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖进行现场对话，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mamdani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·马姆达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews at nytimes.com and in the Times app on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 以及《纽约时报》App 上直播部分访谈。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 今天的主题是阿富汗。

sentences.en: It was barely mentioned in this year's election.
sentences.zh: 在今年的选举中，这个话题几乎被遗忘。

sentences.en: But while U.S.
sentences.zh: 但就在美国

sentences.en: attention has turned from the Taliban to ISIS, the Taliban is back, stronger than ever, and the government is on the brink of collapse.
sentences.zh: 的注意力从塔利班转向 ISIS 之际，塔利班卷土重来，比以往任何时候都更加强大，而政府也走到了崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: The view from the streets of Kabul and from the Pentagon.
sentences.zh: 喀布尔街头与五角大楼的视角。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, June 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月7日，星期三。

sentences.en: I mean, my parents, they have these images.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的父母，他们脑海里有着这样的画面。

sentences.en: They have these experiences that they talk about of a different Kabul in the 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 他们有着那些经历，谈论着60和70年代那个不同的喀布尔。

sentences.en: Of concerts, open concerts, of cinemas, of coffee shops, of rooftop bars.
sentences.zh: 有音乐会、露天音乐会、电影院、咖啡馆、露天屋顶酒吧。

sentences.en: My colleague, Mujib Mashal, grew up in Kabul and is now a reporter there.
sentences.zh: 我的同事穆吉卜·马沙尔在喀布尔长大，现在是那里的记者。

sentences.en: They have a nostalgia for that past that increasingly it seems imaginary to me because I just cannot connect that nostalgia they have with the current reality.
sentences.zh: 他们对那个过去怀有一种怀旧之情，以至于现在这种情怀在我看来愈发虚幻，因为我实在无法把他们怀念的过去同现实联系起来。

sentences.en: I think the way we describe life in the cities, it's almost become a game of chance.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们描述城市生活的方式，几乎成了一场碰运气游戏。

sentences.en: And some days, some people are just not lucky.
sentences.zh: 有时候，有些人就是没那么幸运。

sentences.en: In the countryside, every month, every day, you hear stories of a wedding convoy over an IED.
sentences.zh: 在乡村，每个月、每一天，你都会听到婚礼车队轧上简易爆炸装置的故事。

sentences.en: Just the beginning of new life, ended before it's even started.
sentences.zh: 一个新生命的起点，甚至还没开始就结束了。

sentences.en: There's no front line to this war.
sentences.zh: 这场战争没有前线。

sentences.en: But the front line could be in front of your office, it could be as you're leaving home, it could be at the bus stop,
sentences.zh: 但前线可能就在你办公室门前，可能在你出门的时候，可能在公交车站，

sentences.en: it could be at the market where you're buying your groceries.
sentences.zh: 可能在你买菜的市场里。

sentences.en: Any moment, any day, anywhere around the city is a possibility of something like this happening.
sentences.zh: 在城市的任何角落，任何一天，任何时刻，都有可能发生这样的事。

sentences.en: On our right is just a full row of tall blast walls.
sentences.zh: 我们的右边是一整排高大的防爆墙。

sentences.en: So my family lives north of the city.
sentences.zh: 我的家人住在城北。

sentences.en: And our offices, the New York Times Bureau, is right in the diplomatic quarter of the city.
sentences.zh: 而我们的办公室，《纽约时报》分社，正好在城市的使馆区。

sentences.en: And over the blast wall is sort of razor wire.
sentences.zh: 防爆墙上方挂着某种带刺的铁丝网。

sentences.en: And then there are three roads that lead to our offices.
sentences.zh: 通往我们办公室的有三条路。

sentences.en: The middle road is the British Embassy.
sentences.zh: 中间那条路通往英国大使馆。

sentences.en: Too many security checks.
sentences.zh: 安全检查太多了。

sentences.en: We sometimes avoid that because it just takes a long time.
sentences.zh: 我们有时会避开那条路，因为太耗时间了。

sentences.en: And they check the car for explosives before they allow us in the parking.
sentences.zh: 而且他们会在允许我们进入停车场之前检查车上有没有爆炸物。

sentences.en: And it leaves us two side roads.
sentences.zh: 这就剩下两条小路了。

sentences.en: It was one of those three roads that were blown up, that killed about 100 people last week.
sentences.zh: 上周发生爆炸、造成约100人死亡的，正是这三条路中的其中一条。

sentences.en: A devastating suicide truck bombing in Kabul.
sentences.zh: 喀布尔发生了一起毁灭性的卡车自杀式炸弹袭击。

sentences.en: In the early morning hours, the massive truck bomb ripping through what is supposed to be one of the most secure parts of Kabul.
sentences.zh: 清晨时分，这枚威力巨大的卡车炸弹炸穿了本该是喀布尔最安全的地带之一。

sentences.en: The blast so powerful, it shattered windows a mile away.
sentences.zh: 爆炸威力如此巨大，以至于一英里外的窗户都被震碎了。

sentences.en: Buildings were leveled.
sentences.zh: 建筑被夷为平地。

sentences.en: Bodies scattered.
sentences.zh: 尸体散落各处。

sentences.en: Cars incinerated.
sentences.zh: 汽车被烧成灰烬。

sentences.en: And just the sheer size of explosion was so big that the windows of our office were all gone, all smashed.
sentences.zh: 爆炸的规模实在太大，以至于我们办公室的窗户全都没了，全都粉碎了。

sentences.en: Of the Times Bureau.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》分社的窗户。

sentences.en: Of the Times Bureau.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》分社的。

sentences.en: And what it makes me think of is that every day that we would drive up through that street, there were about four policemen who would sort of look at our car.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，每天我们开车经过那条街时，大约有四个警察会打量我们的车。

sentences.en: We would enter through that street many times.
sentences.zh: 我们曾多次从那条街进出。

sentences.en: And they would just smile and just pass us through.
sentences.zh: 他们总是微微一笑，然后放我们过去。

sentences.en: Those guys are gone.
sentences.zh: 那些人已经不在了。

sentences.en: Four guys with AK-47s for $200 a month.
sentences.zh: 四个拿着 AK-47、月薪200美元的伙计。

sentences.en: That's what they make.
sentences.zh: 他们就挣这点钱。

sentences.en: Trying to stop a truck full of explosives.
sentences.zh: 试图拦下一辆满载炸药的卡车。

sentences.en: And I think about that image.
sentences.zh: 每当我想起那个画面。

sentences.en: Those four guys, I know that they haven't even found their pieces.
sentences.zh: 那四个小伙子，我知道甚至连他们的尸块都没有找到。

sentences.en: They evaporated.
sentences.zh: 他们灰飞烟灭了。

sentences.en: They haven't even traced anything that's left of them.
sentences.zh: 甚至连他们留下的任何痕迹都找不到。

sentences.en: What's unfolded in Kabul since this attack that you described?
sentences.zh: 在你描述的这次袭击之后，喀布尔又发生了什么？

sentences.en: Two days after the attack, there's a protest that gathered at the explosion site.
sentences.zh: 袭击发生两天后，爆炸地点聚集了一场抗议活动。

sentences.en: It started small, a few hundred people.
sentences.zh: 规模一开始很小，只有几百人。

sentences.en: They were basically critical of the government for not protecting against such a massive security breach.
sentences.zh: 他们主要批评政府未能防范如此大规模的安全漏洞。

sentences.en: But as the protest grew, it became more tense.
sentences.zh: 但随着抗议人群增加，气氛变得更加紧张。

sentences.en: The police start firing.
sentences.zh: 警察开始开枪。

sentences.en: They're basically chasing the crowds right now.
sentences.zh: 他们目前基本上在驱赶人群。

sentences.en: People are running.
sentences.zh: 人们在奔跑。

sentences.en: They're military vehicles.
sentences.zh: 有军用车辆。

sentences.en: So we're adding gunfire is continuing.
sentences.zh: 枪声仍在继续。

sentences.en: Initially, it's they're firing in the air.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们是朝天鸣枪。

sentences.en: But we see video evidence.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到了视频证据。

sentences.en: We see pictures that the guns are actually not pointed at the air, that they are sort of at a lower angle.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的画面显示，枪口实际上并没有朝向天空，而是压得比较低。

sentences.en: And it leaves seven people dead.
sentences.zh: 这导致了七人死亡。

sentences.en: Jeez.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So this is this is a protest that turns into a riot.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场演变成暴乱的抗议。

sentences.en: And it sounds like its original purpose was to seek greater security, greater security and to express sort of solidarity with the casualties.
sentences.zh: 听起来它最初的目的是为了寻求更多安全保障，争取更多安全，并表达对遇难者的某种声援。

sentences.en: And the next day at the funeral of one of the protesters, ministers, political leaders, they all gathered and boom, another explosion.
sentences.zh: 第二天，在其中一名抗议者的葬礼上，部长们、政治领袖们全都聚集在一起，轰的一声，又发生了另一次爆炸。

sentences.en: The dead body is left there on the ground before even it's buried.
sentences.zh: 甚至在下葬之前，尸体就被留在了地上。

sentences.en: 20 other people drop around him.
sentences.zh: 他周围又有20人倒下。

sentences.en: Just as a reminder.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个提醒。

sentences.en: So the reason the United States invaded Afghanistan 15 years ago was pretty explicitly to stamp out the Taliban and to stamp them out because of the belief that they had harbored terrorists who were involved in the September 11th attacks in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国在15年前入侵阿富汗的原因，非常明确地是为了铲除塔利班，铲除他们的原因在于人们相信他们庇护了参与美国“9·11”袭击的恐怖分子。

sentences.en: So what's happened to the Taliban since then?
sentences.zh: 那么自那以后，塔利班怎么了？

sentences.en: Initially, once the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最初，一旦美国

sentences.en: started using force, the Taliban were willing to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 开始使用武力，塔利班是愿意谈判的。

sentences.en: This is 2001, 2002 we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是2001年、2002年的事。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: said, no, we're going to come after every single one of you.
sentences.zh: 说，不，我们要把你们赶尽杀绝。

sentences.en: And they did.
sentences.zh: 他们也确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And for a few years, they had the upper hand, the Americans and the Afghan government, except once the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在头几年里，美国人和阿富汗政府占了上风，直到美国

sentences.en: shifted its attention to Iraq with the invasion of Iraq, the Taliban used that opportunity to regroup.
sentences.zh: 随着入侵伊拉克而将注意力转移到伊拉克，塔利班利用这个机会重新集结。

sentences.en: And 15 years later, they're probably more powerful than they were in 2001 in terms of how much damage they can cause, how much violence they can wage,
sentences.zh: 15年后的今天，就他们能够造成的破坏程度、能够发动的暴力规模而言，

sentences.en: and how much they threaten the survival of the local government in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 以及他们对各省地方政府生存构成的威胁程度来说，他们可能比2001年时更加强大。

sentences.en: How is it possible that they are more powerful now after the United States and the Allied forces sought and seem to be on the way toward basically decimating them and their power?
sentences.zh: 为什么在美国和盟军寻求并似乎即将彻底消灭他们及其势力之后，他们现在反而更强大了？

sentences.en: That's the biggest frustration.
sentences.zh: 这才是最让人沮丧的地方。

sentences.en: The Taliban are numbered at about 30,000 to 40,000 fighters, 30,000 to 40,000.
sentences.zh: 塔利班的武装人员大约有3万到4万人，3万到4万。

sentences.en: On the Afghan government side, you've got about 330,000, 40,000 forces.
sentences.zh: 而在阿富汗政府方面，你拥有大约33万到40万的兵力。

sentences.en: Add to that about 10,000 coalition forces, Americans, NATO.
sentences.zh: 再加上大约1万名联军部队，包括美国人和北约部队。

sentences.en: That math is very lopsided.
sentences.zh: 这个数学对比非常悬殊。

sentences.en: And you look at the fact that last year, 2016, the Afghan forces lost about 20,000 men.
sentences.zh: 然而你看看这个事实：去年，即2016年，阿富汗安全部队损失了大约2万人。

sentences.en: That means they have a remarkable rate of regenerating every year.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们每年都有惊人的兵员补充率。

sentences.en: How does that happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How do you regenerate about 70% of your force year after year?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能年复一年地补充大约70%的兵力？

sentences.en: It boggles my mind.
sentences.zh: 这让我大惑不解。

sentences.en: I don't know the answer to this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道答案是什么。

sentences.en: But not only do they regenerate every year, they keep on striking harder.
sentences.zh: 但他们不仅每年都能补充兵力，而且袭击一次比一次猛烈。

sentences.en: But you've got other actors now.
sentences.zh: 不过现在你们有了其他参与者。

sentences.en: You've got affiliates of the Islamic State who are claiming some of these attacks.
sentences.zh: 伊斯国（ISIS）的分支声称对其中一些袭击负责。

sentences.en: The latest one, nobody has claimed yet.
sentences.zh: 最近的一次袭击，还没有人认领。

sentences.en: The big one that killed about 100 people.
sentences.zh: 那起造成约100人死亡的大型袭击。

sentences.en: But there's a massive gray area also between the Taliban and the Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 但在塔利班和伊斯兰国之间，也存在着一个巨大的灰色地带。

sentences.en: A lot of the Islamic State are local fighters.
sentences.zh: 许多伊斯兰国成员都是当地武装分子。

sentences.en: They're former Taliban from Pakistan, from Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他们是来自巴基斯坦、阿富汗的前塔利班成员。

sentences.en: So the battlefield is getting complicated also in terms of the number of groups operating.
sentences.zh: 因此，从活跃的组织数量来看，战场也变得复杂起来。

sentences.en: This situation that you're describing, which does sound really complicated, can you put it into a larger context for me within Afghanistan's history?
sentences.zh: 你所描述的这种局势听起来确实非常复杂，你能把它放在阿富汗历史的更大背景中为我做个梳理吗？

sentences.en: Well, Afghanistan, it's been a battleground for clashing ideas for a long time during the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在英国殖民时期，阿富汗长期以来一直是各种思想碰撞的战场。

sentences.en: We were the buffer between the Russian Empire and the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 我们曾是俄罗斯帝国与大英帝国之间的缓冲区。

sentences.en: When the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当美国

sentences.en: became sort of the center of the Western world, and then opposing it was communism, we became the clashing ground for those two ideas also.
sentences.zh: 成为西方世界的中心、其对立面是共产主义时，我们也成了这两种思想交锋的角斗场。

sentences.en: So that was a place to bloody the communist's nose.
sentences.zh: 所以这里成了给共产主义者一点颜色看看的地方。

sentences.en: And what happened in the process was that it destabilized what was a pretty relatively stable Afghanistan, actually.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中发生的事情是，它打破了原本相当稳定、实际上还算稳定的阿富汗的局势。

sentences.en: Destabilized it, created new actors.
sentences.zh: 打破了稳定，催生了新的势力。

sentences.en: And one of those actors was, of course, the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 而其中一支势力，当然就是塔利班。

sentences.en: Well, the Taliban was sort of the, grew out of those original actors, because the original actors were created in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，塔利班某种程度上是从最初的那些势力中滋生出来的，因为最初的势力是在70年代创建的。

sentences.en: But the Taliban traced their ideological source to the religious schools in Pakistan that were funded by CIA money to create this ideological opposition to communism.
sentences.zh: 但塔利班的意识形态根源可以追溯到巴基斯坦的宗教学校，这些学校由中情局资金资助，旨在建立对共产主义的意识形态对抗。

sentences.en: Once the Soviets were defeated, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 苏军战败后，美国

sentences.en: packed up and left, only to return after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 收拾行囊离开，直到“9·11”之后才卷土重来。

sentences.en: This map you're laying out, it feels like you have, on one side, the insurgents, Taliban, ISIS.
sentences.zh: 你勾勒出的这幅图景，感觉就像是一边是叛乱分子、塔利班、ISIS。

sentences.en: On the other, you have this problem-plagued government.
sentences.zh: 而在另一边，则是这个麻烦重重的政府。

sentences.en: And then you have the United States forces which back this really problematic government.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有支持这个极其糟糕的政府的美军。

sentences.en: In the eyes of Afghans who are living through all this, who is to blame for the current woes?
sentences.zh: 在亲历这一切的阿富汗人眼中，谁该为当前的困境负责？

sentences.en: Who do they see as the person most responsible?
sentences.zh: 他们认为谁是罪魁祸首？

sentences.en: What is very clear when I travel to the countryside, when I go to the villages, there are parts of the country that every couple months, it switches hands.
sentences.zh: 当我前往乡村、走进村庄时，情况非常明了：有些地方每隔几个月就会易手。

sentences.en: There are districts, there are villages that for a week, it's the government controlling, and then two weeks later, it's Taliban.
sentences.zh: 有些地区、有些村庄，这周由政府控制，两周后又成了塔利班的天下。

sentences.en: It goes back and forth, back and forth.
sentences.zh: 来来回回，反反复复。

sentences.en: They get trampled by both sides.
sentences.zh: 他们被双方无情践踏。

sentences.en: And it almost no longer makes a difference to them anymore.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这几乎已经没有什么区别了。

sentences.en: Because what was promised to them in 2001 is a better alternative to the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 因为2001年承诺给他们的，是一个比塔利班更好的选择。

sentences.en: Democracy, rights, economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 民主、权利、经济繁荣。

sentences.en: All those ideals have faded now.
sentences.zh: 所有这些理想现在都已破灭。

sentences.en: So they, on the one hand, they get the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 所以，一方面，他们迎来了塔利班。

sentences.en: They're brutal.
sentences.zh: 他们残暴。

sentences.en: They're violent.
sentences.zh: 他们充满暴力。

sentences.en: On this side, they get the government.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，他们迎来了政府。

sentences.en: It's corrupt.
sentences.zh: 它腐败。

sentences.en: It's fighting each other.
sentences.zh: 内部争权夺利。

sentences.en: And when they come take over, they can't defend their area.
sentences.zh: 当塔利班攻占过来时，他们根本无力保卫自己的地区。

sentences.en: So they leave it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们抛弃了这里。

sentences.en: They leave the local population vulnerable to the Taliban again.
sentences.zh: 他们让当地民众再次置于塔利班的威胁之下。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of blame to be thrown around.
sentences.zh: 所以有太多的指责可以归咎于各方。

sentences.en: But what is very evident, very clear, is just the suffering of the local people.
sentences.zh: 但非常明显、非常确凿的是，当地人民正在承受苦难。

sentences.en: Do Afghans feel that this war has been forgotten by the United States?
sentences.zh: 阿富汗人觉得这场战争被美国遗忘了嘛？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: Because when you look back at the elections, it was not even mentioned more than once or twice.
sentences.zh: 因为当你回看那些选举时，它甚至连一两次都没被提及。

sentences.en: In the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国

sentences.en: presidential election.
sentences.zh: 总统选举中。

sentences.en: And people are watching very closely.
sentences.zh: 大家其实一直在密切关注。

sentences.en: We go back to that idea of a cycle.
sentences.zh: 我们又回到了那种循环的观念。

sentences.en: This war has been a cycle.
sentences.zh: 这场战争一直是一个循环。

sentences.en: And they thought the American election could be another refresher of attention.
sentences.zh: 他们本以为美国大选能再次唤起人们的关注。

sentences.en: But it was not even mentioned.
sentences.zh: 但它甚至都没被提起。

sentences.en: So how do you personally feel about the war 16 years later as somebody who grew up there?
sentences.zh: 那么作为一个在那里长大的人，16年后你个人对这场战争有什么感受？

sentences.en: It's the uncertainty that 16 years later, and as a reporter, I have a closer, deeper look at the uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不确定性，16年过去了，作为一名记者，我对这种不确定性有了更近、更深的观察。

sentences.en: The average person may think that there's some solution being worked at secretly, that we don't see it.
sentences.zh: 普通人可能会觉得有什么解决方案正在暗中推进，只是我们看不到。

sentences.en: I would imagine that.
sentences.zh: 我会这样设想。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But what disappoints me is, as a reporter, the deeper I dig, the more I don't see it.
sentences.zh: 但让我失望的是，作为一名记者，我挖得越深，就越看不到这一点。

sentences.en: So as an Afghan, but also as a reporter, when I look deeper into it, and I don't see much,
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个阿富汗人，同时也是一名记者，当我更深入地探究却发现没多少实质内容时，

sentences.en: the uncertainty comes off the back of 15 years of a lot of international money that went in, a lot of lives lost, both Afghan and international coalition.
sentences.zh: 这种不确定性是在过去15年大量国际资金涌入、无数阿富汗人和国际联军生命消逝的背景下产生的。

sentences.en: And the attention is exhausted.
sentences.zh: 而且大家的关注度已经耗尽了。

sentences.en: Over the past 15 years, it was NATO, the U.S., the whole world was paying attention to where is this country going to go.
sentences.zh: 在过去15年里，北约、美国、全世界都在关注这个国家将走向何方。

sentences.en: Now I think it's coming to a moment where the light at the end of the tunnel is so dim.
sentences.zh: 现在我认为，隧道尽头的微光已经变得极其黯淡。

sentences.en: And that's what complicates trying to look ahead as to what could be the end of this conflict.
sentences.zh: 这就让试图展望这场冲突将如何结束变得复杂起来。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the president's press secretary, Sean Spicer, got a rare question about the White House's thinking on Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 周二，总统新闻秘书肖恩·斯派塞被问到一个罕见的问题，关于白宫对阿富汗问题的考量。

sentences.en: Before the foreign trip, the president's first foreign trip, senior officials were telling us that you guys would unveil the results of the Afghan review
sentences.zh: 在这次国事访问、总统首次出访之前，高级官员曾告诉我们，你们会在

sentences.en: and the president's decision-making after the foreign trip.
sentences.zh: 国事访问结束后公布阿富汗政策审查的结果以及总统的决策。

sentences.en: Do you have a timeline for us?
sentences.zh: 你们能给我们一个时间表吗？

sentences.en: When can we expect this announcement?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候能期待这个宣布？

sentences.en: I think the president will continue to discuss that with Secretary Mattis, General McMaster, and others,
sentences.zh: 我认为总统会继续与马蒂斯部长、麦克马斯特将军及其他人讨论这个问题，

sentences.en: and when he feels as though he's comfortable with a plan that he wants to push forward, we'll let you know.
sentences.zh: 当他觉得对想要推进的计划感到满意时，我们会通知你们的。

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我毫无头绪。

sentences.en: I do not begin to know what President Trump thinks about Afghanistan, if he's even thought about Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道特朗普总统对阿富汗是怎么想的，甚至不知道他是否考虑过阿富汗。

sentences.en: My colleague Helene Cooper covers the Pentagon for The Times.
sentences.zh: 我的同事海伦·库珀为《时报》报道五角大楼新闻。

sentences.en: With Obama, it was much easier.
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马时期，这要容易得多。

sentences.en: He was definitely a non-interventionist, and he wanted a timeline on how long he wanted American troops in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是个不干涉主义者，他希望为美国军队在阿富汗驻留多久设定一个时间表。

sentences.en: And a lot of people at the Pentagon believe that those parameters sort of doomed us to fail in Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 五角大楼的许多人认为，这些条条框框在某种程度上注定了我们在阿富汗的失败，

sentences.en: because as long as you tell the warring groups in Afghanistan that we're going to be getting out no matter what in X amount of time, all they have to do is wait us out.
sentences.zh: 因为只要你告诉阿富汗的交战各方，无论如何我们都会在某个时间期限内撤离，他们唯一需要做的就是跟我们耗下去。

sentences.en: So you said we don't know what President Trump thinks about Afghanistan, but do we have any idea what his military advisors want?
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才说我们不知道特朗普总统对阿富汗的看法，那我们知不知道他的军事顾问们想要什么？

sentences.en: They want at least 5,000 more troops.
sentences.zh: 他们至少想要增兵5000人。

sentences.en: They want to help continue to train the Afghan security forces,
sentences.zh: 他们希望继续帮助训练阿富汗安全部队，

sentences.en: and building up the Afghanistan military is sort of one of those things that the Pentagon believes that we have to do
sentences.zh: 壮大阿富汗军队是五角大楼认为我们必须要做的事情之一，

sentences.en: if there's going to be any chance of getting them strong enough that they can then sort of strong-arm the Taliban
sentences.zh: 如果还有任何机会让阿富汗军队变得足够强大，从而能够以强势姿态迫使塔利班

sentences.en: to the reconciliation table and work out some sort of political reconciliation.
sentences.zh: 坐到和谈桌前，达成某种政治和解的话。

sentences.en: And that's what the Pentagon believes they need to do to take away this we're about to pull out type of mentality.
sentences.zh: 这就是五角大楼认为他们需要做的事情，用来消除那种“我们马上就要撤军”的心态。

sentences.en: They want to give the impression that, look, we're here to stay.
sentences.zh: 他们想给人一种印象：听着，我们是来长久驻留的。

sentences.en: We're invested in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们对这个国家进行了投入。

sentences.en: We're going to be here as long as it takes.
sentences.zh: 只要需要，我们会一直待在这里。

sentences.en: And how has the emergence of ISIS in Afghanistan changed the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么伊斯兰国（ISIS）在阿富汗的出现，是否改变了美军

sentences.en: approach on the ground, if it has?
sentences.zh: 在当地的方针，如果有改变的话？

sentences.en: It's helped make the general's plea for more troops a little bit more strident.
sentences.zh: 它让将军们要求增兵的呼吁变得更加强烈了一些。

sentences.en: The generals, the American generals there can now say, look, we've got to make sure that we stop the spread of ISIS,
sentences.zh: 那里的美国将军们现在可以说了，听着，我们必须确保阻止伊斯兰国蔓延，

sentences.en: and now they're in Afghanistan, which is why they're hoping to get up to 5,000 more troops.
sentences.zh: 而他们现在已经进入了阿富汗，这就是为什么他们希望能增兵多达5000人。

sentences.en: And I think what the Pentagon wants is to get to a point where the various groups in Afghanistan don't expect that they can wait out the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为五角大楼想要的是达到这样一个地步：阿富汗各方不再指望能够把美国给耗走。

sentences.en: Is there a consensus within the military that having more troops in Afghanistan is a good idea?
sentences.zh: 军方内部对于在阿富汗增兵是否是个好主意有没有共识？

sentences.en: There's a big difference between what the generals believe and are asking for and the rank and file.
sentences.zh: 将军们的信念和诉求与普通基层官兵之间存在很大差异。

sentences.en: A lot of the rank and file question, and you're talking everybody from Marines to Navy SEALs to Army infantry, what are we still doing there?
sentences.zh: 许多基层官兵——从海军陆战队员到海豹突击队员再到陆军步兵，都在质问：我们到底还在那里干什么？

sentences.en: You know, I keep forgetting the name of this Brad Pitt movie that's out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我总是记不起布拉德·皮特上映的那部电影叫什么名字。

sentences.en: We are here to build a war machine.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里是为了打造一台战争机器。

sentences.en: To support the civilian population.
sentences.zh: 为了支持平民百姓。

sentences.en: To that end, you must avoid killing it at all costs.
sentences.zh: 为此，你不惜一切代价也要避免杀死平民。

sentences.en: And it's so weird because everybody at the Pentagon is talking about it, and it's a very anti-Afghanistan war movie.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了，因为五角大楼每个人都在讨论它，这是一部非常反阿富汗战争的电影。

sentences.en: I haven't seen it yet, but I've read reviews of it, and the guys who you think would be offended by it love it.
sentences.zh: 我还没看过，但我读过它的评论，而那些你以为会被它冒犯的军人却很喜欢它。

sentences.en: It's amazing to me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: So many of them have lost, you know, colleagues, they've lost fellow soldiers, and are constantly asking, what are we still doing there, and what are we fighting for?
sentences.zh: 他们当中有很多人失去了同事，失去了战友，并且不断在问，我们到底还在那里干什么？我们在为什么而战？

sentences.en: But at the same time, you have these officers who say, you know, we've lost all of these people in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你又会听到这些军官说，你知道的，我们在阿富汗失去了这么多的人。

sentences.en: We've spent so much blood and treasure on the ground in that country, and then you just turn around and pull out.
sentences.zh: 我们在那个国家的土地上花费了那么多的鲜血和财富，然后你拍拍屁股就撤走。

sentences.en: Again, then you get the, what was that for?
sentences.zh: 这样一来，你又会面临这样的质疑：这一切究竟是为了什么？

sentences.en: So it's a contradiction at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以这同时也是一种矛盾。

sentences.en: But the rank and file are always going to follow order, so.
sentences.zh: 但基层官兵总是会服从命令的，所以。

sentences.en: Is the possibility, Holina, of actually leaving an option being discussed within the U.S.
sentences.zh: 海伦，彻底离开的可能性，也就是直接撤出阿富汗，是否正在美国

sentences.en: military, just getting out of Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 军方内部进行讨论？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: We can't just leave completely because, you know, the second you have some sort of attack on the United States homeland or one of our allies that can be traced back to Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 我们不能就这么彻底离开，因为你知道的，一旦美国本土或我们的盟友遭到某种可以追溯到阿富汗的袭击，

sentences.en: you're going to have people going right back in there.
sentences.zh: 人们马上就会重新杀回那里。

sentences.en: And that's one of the reasons why.
sentences.zh: 这就是原因之一。

sentences.en: Let's say the Taliban takes over Afghanistan again.
sentences.zh: 假设塔利班再次接管阿富汗。

sentences.en: You no longer then have a government that's at the very least, even if they're weak and even if they're completely useless, is at least your ally and sharing intelligence with,
sentences.zh: 你就再也没有这样一个政府了：它至少（哪怕它很软弱、哪怕它完全无能）还是你的盟友，能与你共享情报，

sentences.en: and you're able to come and go as you please.
sentences.zh: 并且能让你随时自由出入。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's one of the things I think because counterterrorism is such a big deal and Americans have become so skittish about attacks here,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为正是因为反恐是如此重大的事情，美国人对本土遭受袭击变得如此神经质，

sentences.en: I don't see how we ever actually managed to leave Afghanistan because people are not going to forget September 11 that easily.
sentences.zh: 我看不出我们怎么可能真正做到离开阿富汗，因为人们不会那么轻易忘记“9·11”。

sentences.en: Helene, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 海伦，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 真的非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: President Trump is claiming credit for a decision by five Arab countries, including Egypt and Saudi Arabia, to sever diplomatic and economic ties to the nation of Qatar,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统正将沙特阿拉伯和埃及等五个阿拉伯国家宣布与卡塔尔断绝外交和经济关系归功于自己的决定，

sentences.en: citing its support for terrorist groups.
sentences.zh: 这些国家给出的理由是卡塔尔支持恐怖组织。

sentences.en: During my recent trip to the Middle East, the president said on Twitter,
sentences.zh: 总统在推特上写道，在我最近访问中东期间，

sentences.en: I stated that there can no longer be funding of radical ideology.
sentences.zh: 我曾表示绝不能再资助激进意识形态。

sentences.en: Leaders pointed to Qatar.
sentences.zh: 各国领导人将矛头指向了卡塔尔。

sentences.en: That message from the president surprised U.S.
sentences.zh: 总统的这一表态让美国

sentences.en: military leaders.
sentences.zh: 军方领导人大吃一惊。

sentences.en: Qatar is a U.S.
sentences.zh: 卡塔尔是美国的

sentences.en: ally, a partner in the fight against ISIS, and a crucial military outpost for the United States, with 10,000 American troops stationed there.
sentences.zh: 盟友、打击“伊斯兰国”的伙伴，也是美国至关重要的军事据点，有1万名美军驻扎在那里。

sentences.en: And the Times is reporting that before he was fired by the president,
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，在被总统解职之前，

sentences.en: FBI Director James Comey asked Attorney General Jeff Sessions to make sure he would never again be left alone with the president.
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局（FBI）局长詹姆士·科米曾要求司法部长杰夫·塞申斯确保以后绝不再让他单独与总统共处一室。

sentences.en: That request came in February, the day after Comey says that Trump brought him into the Oval Office and asked him to end the FBI investigation
sentences.zh: 这一请求是在2月份提出的，就在科米所说的特朗普将他召入椭圆形办公室、并要求他结束联邦调查局

sentences.en: into National Security Advisor Michael Flynn's ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 对国家安全顾问迈克尔·弗林与俄罗斯关系的调查的第二天。

sentences.en: Comey reportedly did not tell Sessions, his boss at the time, about that conversation with Trump, an omission that Comey is expected to be asked about
sentences.zh: 据报道，科米当时并没有将与特朗普的这次谈话告诉他的顶头上司塞申斯，科米预计将在周四

sentences.en: when he testifies before the Senate on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 在参议院作证时被问及这一疏忽。

sentences.en: Finally, the Times is reporting that the relationship between Sessions and President Trump has grown so tense that Sessions suggested he could resign as Attorney General.
sentences.zh: 最后，《时报》报道称，塞申斯与特朗普总统之间的关系已经变得如此紧张，以至于塞申斯暗示他可能会辞去司法部长职务。

sentences.en: President Trump remains angry at Sessions for recusing himself from the Justice Department's Russia investigation back in March.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统仍然对塞申斯在今年3月主动回避司法部的俄罗斯调查感到愤怒。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。
